hook: Defect-rich cerium MOFs use plain oxygen to break down pollutants, holding over 90% BPA removal for 48 h
hook_turn: holding over 90% BPA removal for 48 h
summary: Bulky organic linkers were used to create missing-linker defects and oxygen vacancies in a cerium MOF, letting it turn oxygen into superoxide radicals that destroy contaminants without added energy. A membrane flow system kept removal of bisphenol A above 90% for 48 h. Only a few model pollutants were tested, not real wastewater.
title: Linker Steric Hindrance-Induced Defect Engineering Enables Oxygen Vacancy-Rich MOFs for Pollutant Degradation
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
